name: FindThatSoftware (FTS)

sources.title: Vendor page — 'List your software for Indian buyers'; free to apply, editorial floor: a buyer must be able to try and evaluate the product today (content read via search index; direct fetch returned HTTP 429)
About — vendors submit or correct listings on the vendor page; corrections free; monetized by affiliate links and labelled paid placements
Homepage — 296 tools across 41 categories; source-backed listings with verified India pricing

conditions: Free to apply, but listings are editorially reviewed — 'we only ever feature tools we would genuinely recommend'
Hard floor: 'a buyer must be able to try and evaluate your product today' — a public trial/free tier or evaluable product
Pricing must be discoverable (published or clearly obtainable) — they compute an all-in India cost
The vendor site must be 'source-backable': enough public feature/pricing/support detail to cite
requirements: Software products evaluable by Indian buyers — 296 tools across 41 categories indexed
Early independent makers explicitly welcome — 'no traction, funding, or big brand needed'
Real published/obtainable pricing required for the all-in India cost calculation
Public site must substantiate claims — listings carry visible source URLs and last-checked dates
preparation: Product name, URL, and a working public trial/free tier or demo
Public pricing page or clearly stated price
Feature, pricing, and support documentation the editors can cite
India-relevant notes if applicable (INR pricing, GST handling, regional availability)
workflow: Open https://findthatsoftware.com/vendors ('List your software for Indian buyers')
Submit or correct the listing via the vendor page — corrections are always free and never affect rankings
Editors compile a source-backed listing with verified India pricing
Paid vendor placements exist but are labelled and do not buy rankings
watchFor: Direct fetches returned HTTP 429 repeatedly — the site rate-limits automated access; use a real browser and expect blocks
India-buyer focus — listings emphasize 'all-in India cost'; a product with no India story may get less value
Editorial bar is real: 'if we would not recommend a tool to a buyer regardless of pay, it does not get listed'
Corrections go through the vendor page; buyer-side issues through the buying-help form
countsAsLive: The product appears in the findthatsoftware.com catalog under its category with a source-backed listing showing India pricing and a last-checked date
unknowns: Exact submission form fields — direct fetch was blocked by 429 on every attempt
Pricing for the labelled paid placements
